signal.title: [Serve] Orphan ProxyActor left ALIVE when proxy shutdown times out under heavy controller load (blocks worker scale-down)
signal.text: ### What happened + What you expected to happen **Bug** On a large Ray Serve cluster (~381 applications / many `DeploymentHandle`s), the Serve controller repeatedly logs: ```text ERROR ... controller ... -- Exception updating proxy state. Traceback (most recent call last): File ".../ray/serve/_private/controller.py", line 607, in run_control_loop_step self.proxy_state_manager.update(proxy_nodes=self._proxy_nodes) File ".../ray/serve/_private/proxy_state.py", line 781, in update self._stop_proxies_if_needed() File ".../ray/serve/_private/proxy_state.py", line 982, in _stop_proxies_if_needed proxy_state.shutdown() File ".../ray/serve/_private/proxy_state.py", line 567, in shutdown self._actor_proxy_wrapper.kill() File ".../ray/serve/_private/proxy_state.py", line 323, in kill ray.get(shutdown_ref, timeout=5) ... ray.exceptions.GetTimeoutError: Get timed out: some object(s) not ready. ``` After this, worker nodes that should be idle keep an **ALIVE** `ProxyActor` that is **no longer tracked** in `serve.status().proxies`. Those orphan proxies prevent the autoscaler from scaling the workers down. **Expected** When the controller decides to stop a proxy, either: 1. the proxy is gracefully shut down and `ray.kill`'d, **or** 2. if `shutdown.remote()` times out / fails, the actor is still force-killed and not left as an unmanaged ALIVE orphan. `serve.status().proxies` and the set of ALIVE Serve `ProxyActor`s should stay consistent. ### Root cause analysis Two bugs compound under controller overload: #### 1) Half-cleanup in stop/kill path (immediate orphan creator) `_stop_proxies_if_needed` removes the proxy from the manager **before** kill completes: ```python # proxy_state.py (_stop_proxies_if_needed) for node_id in to_stop: proxy_state = self._proxy_states.pop(node_id) # (1) drop from managed state ... proxy_state.shutdown() ``` `ActorProxyWrapper.kill()` then does: ```python shutdown_ref = self._actor_handle.shutdown.remote() ray.get(shutdown_ref, timeout=5) # (2) can raise GetTimeoutError ray.kill(self._actor_handle, no_restart=True) # (3) never reached on timeout ``` The controller control loop catches the exception and continues: ```python # controller.py except Exception: logger.exception("Exception updating proxy state.") ``` Result: | Step | Effect | |---|---| | `pop` succeeded | proxy disappears from `status().proxies` | | `ray.get(shutdown, timeout=5)` timed out | exception aborts `kill()` | | `ray.kill` never runs | actor remains **ALIVE** | | controller forgets the actor | **orphan** → blocks worker idle / scale-down | `ProxyActor.shutdown()` itself is essentially a no-op / very cheap; a 5s timeout strongly suggests RPC / scheduling / controller overload rather than heavy shutdown work. #### 2) Control-loop overload with hundreds of apps (trigger) With ~**381 Serve applications** and a large number of `DeploymentHandle`s, the controller control loop is heavily loaded (metrics / long-poll / proxy health+drain+stop bookkeeping). Under that load, `shutdown.remote()` often cannot complete within 5s, so path (1) fires repeatedly and leaves orphan proxies on workers. This matches the direction of ongoing controller scalability work: - https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/64510 — refresh GCS node-info cache off the control loop (async) - https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/64886 — cache merged autoscaling-metrics timeseries across controller ticks - https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/63144 — `[Serve][RFC] Scaling Autoscaling Metrics Communication in Ray Serve` Related but different open PR that also touches the proxy kill/update path: - https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/64403 — fix proxy update loop stuck on `ActorUnschedulableError` in `is_shutdown()` (exception escape / hang). That does **not** cover the `GetTimeoutError` after `pop` leaving an ALIVE orphan. ### Suggested fixes **Hardening (should fix orphans even under load):** 1. In `ActorProxyWrapper.kill()`, always call `ray.kill(..., no_restart=True)` in a `finally` (or after catching `GetTimeoutError` / other Ray errors), so a timed-out graceful shutdown cannot leave an ALIVE actor. 2. Optionally reverse `_stop_proxies_if_needed` ordering: only `pop` after successful kill, or keep a "stopping" tombstone so a failed stop can be retried instead of forgotten. **Scalability (address the overload trigger):** Continue reducing per-tick control-loop work for large app / handle counts (related: #64510, #64886, #63144). ### Workaround Manually kill ALIVE Serve `ProxyActor`s that are not present in `serve.status().proxies`. Reducing app/handle count or using head-only proxy placement also lowers how often this path is hit. ### Versions / Dependencies - Ray **2.55.0** - Python 3.10 - Large Serve footprint: ~381 applications / many DeploymentHandles on one controller - Observed on a production-like large multi-app cluster; stack traces match `proxy_state.py` / `controller.py` on this version ### Reproduction script Fully minimal local repro is hard because it depends on controller overload, but the failure mode is deterministic from the code path: 1. Deploy many Serve applications (hundreds) so the controller control loop is saturated (metrics / long-poll / proxy management). 2. Trigger proxy stop/drain (scale deployments down, or remove replicas from a worker so the proxy becomes drainable / stoppable). 3. Observe controller logs: `Exception updating proxy state.` with `GetTimeoutError` in `ActorProxyWrapper.kill` at `ray.get(shutdown_ref, timeout=5)`. 4. Compare: - `serve.status().proxies` — node missing - `ray list actors` / actor table — corresponding `ProxyActor` still **ALIVE** 5. Autoscaler / KubeRay does not remove the worker because the orphan proxy keeps the node non-idle. A unit-level repro can patch `ray.get` in `ActorProxyWrapper.kill` to raise `GetTimeoutError` and assert that `ray.kill` is still invoked and/or the proxy remains managed for retry. ### Issue Severity High: It blocks me from completing my task. Worker scale-down is blocked until orphan proxies are cleaned up manually; this is painful on large autoscaled clusters.

signal.title: [core] Unify executor threads when enabling/disabling concurrency_groups
signal.text: ### Description Currently, the main thread is used for system-critical events like dispatching task submission. It is also used for default task execution, as long as concurrency_groups isn't defined. If concurrency_groups is defined, we create a separate executor thread for task execution on the default concurrency group, to avoid blocking task submission to background threads on a task running on the main thread. Ideally, we would use the same codepath no matter whether concurrency_groups is defined or not. ### Use case List of some requirements compiled from various user issues: - Tasks in different concurrency groups should not be blocked from dispatch by each other - Solution: Move control plane logic for task dispatch from main thread to background io event loop - All Python `threading` operations should act as expected, per concurrency group - Ex: threading.Local state should persist across tasks on the same concurrency group. - No crashes during shutdown. - User should be able to run tasks on the main thread - Ex: A non-constructor actor task should be able to install a signal handler - If the default concurrency group has 1 thread, then tasks on the default concurrency group should always run on the main thread - If the user specifies concurrency groups or max_concurrency, there should be a way to specify that a particular task needs to run on the main thread. - Be able to dynamically add a concurrency group - Ex: Needed for the “_ray_system” concurrency group, which handles background operations in Python - Get rid of boost::fiber and all the related hackery (infinitely increasing the python stack frame limit). - There shouldn’t be any surprising behavior when users incrementally update code (for example, add another CG or add an async def method). - For example, currently in Ray, I add one asyncio method and now some other method code breaks because it no longer runs on the main thread.

signal.text: ### What happened + What you expected to happen ## Bug: Iterator invalidation in node label scheduling filter ### Description `NodeLabelSchedulingPolicy::FilterNodesByLabelMatchExpressions` erases entries from an `absl::flat_hash_map` while iterating over it, but the loop continues to increment the erased iterator afterward. Current code: ```cpp for (auto iter = match_nodes.begin(); iter != match_nodes.end(); iter++) { if (!IsNodeMatchLabelExpression(*(iter->second), expression)) { match_nodes.erase(iter); } } After match_nodes.erase(iter), iter is invalidated. The for loop then executes iter++, which increments an invalid iterator. This is undefined behavior. Impact This can cause unstable or incorrect behavior in node label scheduling, including: - Crashes under sanitizer/debug builds. - Skipping entries while filtering candidate nodes. - Leaving non-matching nodes in the candidate set. - Potentially scheduling tasks on nodes that do not satisfy hard node-label constraints. The issue affects node-label scheduling when one or more candidate nodes do not match a hard or soft label expression. Expected behavior Non-matching nodes should be safely removed from the candidate map while preserving valid iteration state. Actual behavior The iterator used for traversal may be invalidated and then incremented, resulting in undefined behavior. Proposed fix Advance the iterator before erasing the current element, for example: for (auto iter = match_nodes.begin(); iter != match_nodes.end();) { if (IsNodeMatchLabelExpression(*(iter->second), expression)) { ++iter; } else { auto iter_to_erase = iter; ++iter; match_nodes.erase(iter_to_erase); } } Suggested regression test Add a test in: src/ray/raylet/scheduling/policy/tests/scheduling_policy_test.cc The test should create multiple feasible nodes that all fail a hard node-label expression, then verify that scheduling returns NodeID::Nil(). Example scenario: - Nodes have label region=us-east. - Scheduling strategy requires hard expression region in ["us-west"]. - Expected result: no matching node, so scheduling returns NodeID::Nil(). Relevant file src/ray/raylet/scheduling/policy/node_label_scheduling_policy.cc ### Versions / Dependencies latest master branch. ### Reproduction script in semantic logically. ### Issue Severity None

signal.title: [Data] Extend StreamingRepartition non-strict fusion to Filter/MapRows/FlatMap
signal.text: ## Why are these changes needed? In non-strict mode, `StreamingRepartition` uses the default pass-through bundler (`ref_bundler=None`): each input block is split independently, with no cross-task buffering and no `batch_size` constraint. Under that semantics, `Filter`/`MapRows`/`FlatMap` are fusion-eligible for exactly the same reason `MapBatches` is — physically all four are `TaskPoolMapOperator`s whose transform chains get concatenated (upstream transform first, then the row-count-based block split), so data semantics are unchanged. Strict mode is untouched: it requires cross-task buffering (`RebundleQueue(ExactMultipleSize(...))`), and `_can_fuse` keeps rejecting non-MapBatches upstreams there (they have no `batch_size` to guarantee divisibility). Closes #63624. This re-implements the design from #63625 (auto-closed as stale) against the current master, with credit to that PR's approach and tests. cc @ray-project/ray-data ## Related issue number Closes #63624 ## Checks - [x] I've signed off every commit (DCO) - [x] I've run `scripts/format.sh` and installed pre-commit hooks - [x] I've added unit tests and verified that all tests pass (this is required) - [x] I've manually verified the change (e.g. via `ds.explain()` on the repro pipeline) ## Tests ```bash python -m pytest -q python/ray/data/tests/test_operator_fusion.py -k streaming_repartition # 17 passed (incl. 9 new: fusion param x4, strict-no-fusion param x4, chain, batch_size semantics) python -m pytest -q python/ray/data/tests/test_repartition_e2e.py -k streaming_repartition # 25 passed (incl. 13 new: fusion param x4, empty-result, full pipeline, partial-empty blocks, # block-shape invariant, target boundaries, single block, empty input, # expr-filter after pushdown, remote-args negative) ruff check / black --check (22.10.0) on the changed files: all passed ``` Additional local verification (not part of the test suite): - 10 read-path scenarios (`read_parquet`/`read_csv`/`read_json` -> filter -> repartition, incl. multi-file, empty file, block-shape invariant, predicate-pushdown interaction): all passed - Performance on 2M rows (read_parquet, 5 files, 100B payload): `filter -> repartition(4096)` goes from **5.97s to 2.18s (~2.7x)**; on 20M rows: **48.1s to 24.1s (2.0x)** — the fused operator avoids an intermediate materialization round-trip Note: 3 pre-existing shuffle-related tests in `test_operator_fusion.py` error locally with `AttributeError: SHUFFLE_V2` (master tests against the installed 2.57.0 build); they are unrelated to this change and pass in CI. ## AI assistance This change was developed with AI assistance (code drafting, test authoring, and review). The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above locally. ## Why this is not a duplicate - Issue #63624 is open with zero comments and no assignee; the only PR referencing it (#63625) was auto-closed as stale without merging and the issue remains unaddressed on master. - No open PRs reference #63624 (checked via `gh pr list --search "63624"`). - The approach differs from the closed PR by adapting to current master (e.g. `AbstractUDFMap` now takes a list of input ops), fixing the PEP 8 lambda issue from #63625's review, extracting a shared fusion-eligibility constant, and adding coverage for empty results, block-shape invariants, the full original pipeline, and read-path scenarios.

(ServeController pid=9590) INFO 2025-02-11 17:24:47,746 controller 9590 -- Replica(id='zle235y2', deployment='A', app='default') did not shut down after grace period, force-killing it. (ServeController pid=9590) INFO 2025-02-11 17:24:47,852 controller 9590 -- Replica(id='zle235y2', deployment='A', app='default') is stopped. ``` Two improvements we should make: - If a replica is completely infeasible in the cluster, we shouldn't continually try to create it but instead fail with `DEPLOY_FAILED`. - If a replica is not yet scheduled, we should immediately "terminate" it by canceling the scheduling.

signal.title: [Serve] Add serve deploy --merge for per application upsert
signal.text: ## Summary Adds a `--merge` mode to `serve deploy` that upserts the submitted applications and leaves all other running applications untouched. Without `--merge`, behavior is unchanged, the config is treated as the full goal state and missing apps are deleted. ## Design - A new `apply_strategy` field on `ServeDeploySchema` accepts `"replace"` (default) or `"merge"`. - Backwards compatible in both directions: old clients default to `replace`, old servers silently ignore the unknown field. - Users activate merge mode via `serve deploy config.yaml --merge` or by setting `apply_strategy: merge` in the YAML. ## Changes - **`schema.py`**: `ApplyStrategy` enum and field on `ServeDeploySchema`. - **`scripts.py`**: `--merge` CLI flag, sets `apply_strategy` before sending config. - **`serve_head.py`**: In merge mode, skips building `http_options`/`grpc_options`/`proxy_location` unless explicitly set, preventing Pydantic defaults from overwriting running cluster options. - **`controller.py`**: Seeds checkpoint from existing apps in merge mode, gates `target_capacity` on `model_fields_set`, passes `delete_missing_apps=False` to the application state manager. - **`application_state.py`**: New `delete_missing_apps` parameter to skip deletion of apps not in the submitted config. - **`usage.proto` and `usage.py`**: `SERVE_REST_API_APPLY_STRATEGY` telemetry tag. - **`multi-app.md`**: User docs for `--merge`. ## Tests - `test_schema.py`: Tests `apply_strategy` enum values and default behavior on `ServeDeploySchema` - `test_cli.py`: Tests `--merge` flag compatibility with import paths, YAML files. - `test_application_state.py`: Tests `delete_missing_apps` parameter across merge, replace, and mixed mode deploys - `test_deploy_app.py`: Tests end-to-end deploy lifecycle with merge and replace mode switching on a live cluster ## Related issues Fixes #63015

signal.title: Llm governance middleware foundation
signal.text: ## Description Adds an alpha governance middleware layer for Ray Serve LLM so users can inspect or block OpenAI-compatible chat, completions, and transcription traffic without changing vLLM or SGLang. `GovernanceIngress` subclasses `OpenAiIngress` and runs an ordered `LLMMiddleware` chain around `_process_llm_request`: - `before_inference` — required. Return the request to proceed, or a `BlockedResponse` to stop before the model is called. - `after_inference` — optional. Sees the full non-streaming response, or the first stream chunk. - `on_inference_complete` — optional. Runs after the response is returned, including after a stream ends, with the last usage dict. Users wire it through the existing `ingress_cls_config` / `ingress_extra_kwargs` on `build_openai_app`. The public API is `ray.serve.llm.governance` (`GovernanceIngress`, `LLMMiddleware`, `RequestContext`, `BlockedResponse`). `BlockedResponse` maps to OpenAI-style JSON errors: `PII_DETECTED` → 400, `BUDGET_EXCEEDED` → 402, `ACCESS_DENIED` → 403, `THROTTLED` → 429 with `Retry-After`. This is the Ray-side hook interface for #65259. Concrete engines (TealTiger, AgentShield, custom policies) live in separate packages and subclass `LLMMiddleware`. Out of scope for this PR: stream buffering / redaction, per-model middleware on `LLMConfig`, embeddings/scoring hooks, and direct streaming (`RAY_SERVE_LLM_ENABLE_DIRECT_STREAMING` already rejects a custom ingress). ## Related issues Related to #65259. ## Additional information ### Usage ```python from ray.serve.llm import LLMConfig, build_openai_app from ray.serve.llm.governance import ( BlockedResponse, GovernanceIngress, LLMMiddleware, ) class DenyModelMiddleware(LLMMiddleware): async def before_inference(self, request, context): if context.model_id == "blocked-model": return BlockedResponse( rule_triggered="ACCESS_DENIED", reason="Model is not allowed", ) return request app = build_openai_app( { "llm_configs": [llm_config], "ingress_cls_config": { "ingress_cls": GovernanceIngress, "ingress_extra_kwargs": { "middlewares": [DenyModelMiddleware()], }, }, } ) ``` Docs: `doc/source/serve/llm/user-guides/governance.md`. ### Tests ```bash python -m pytest python/ray/llm/tests/serve/cpu/governance/ -v ``` Coverage: middleware chain, request-context extraction, reference PII/budget middleware, mocked-handle ingress (block before LLM, 429, stream completion, aclose on block/disconnect), `build_openai_app` wiring, and HTTP e2e through `serve.run` + `httpx` + `MockVLLMEngine`. ### User Guide User guide: `doc/source/serve/llm/user-guides/governance.md` (also linked from the Serve LLM user-guides index and the API reference).

signal.title: [core][dashboard] Return 4xx from node and actor detail APIs
signal.text: ## Description Makes three node/actor dashboard endpoints report client errors with 4xx status codes instead of 200/500. [#51417](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/pull/51417) added the `HTTPStatusCode` enum and the `rest_response(status_code=...)` plumbing, but adoption stalled after one endpoint. Across non-test dashboard source there are currently 28 `OK` and 13 `INTERNAL_ERROR` usages versus only 4 non-500 error codes, all confined to `state_head.py` / `state_api_utils.py`. Backend (`python/ray/dashboard/modules/node/node_head.py`): - `GET /nodes/{node_id}` returned **200 with a near-empty payload** for an unknown node ID, because `DataOrganizer.get_node_info` falls back to `.get(node_id, {})`. Now returns **404**. - `GET /logical/actors/{actor_id}` returned **200 with `detail: null`** for an unknown actor ID, because `get_actor_infos` maps unknown IDs to `None`. Now returns **404**. - `GET /nodes` with an unsupported `view` returned **500**. An unsupported query parameter is a client error, so it now returns **400**. ## Related issues Related to [#51442](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/51442) (umbrella: revisit Ray dashboard API status codes). Since that issue is an umbrella, this PR covers `node_head.py` only, so each module can be reviewed independently. ## Additional information ### Frontend change is required, not incidental The node and actor detail pages surfaced these cases by reading `result === false` out of the **200 response body**. axios rejects on 4xx, so those branches go dead the moment the status code changes, and the pages would sit on "Loading the node infos..." indefinitely with `msg` never updated. The SWR fetchers in `useNodeDetail.ts` and `useActorDetail.ts` now catch the 404 and set the same message they set before, preserving existing UI behavior. Consumers of `useFetchActor` (the Serve pages) already use optional chaining on the result, so returning `undefined` there is unchanged behavior. ### Tests Added `test_node_api_status_codes` (single cluster, looping over all three error paths plus the three success paths — not parametrized, since `ray_start_with_dashboard` starts a fresh cluster per invocation) and `test_actor_not_found_status_code`. Test environment: because Ray's core is compiled, these were run against the Ray Windows nightly wheel built from `3fb63d965f` — the exact base commit of this branch — with the patched `node_head.py` overlaid, so the patch was the only delta. ``` pytest -v python/ray/dashboard/modules/node/tests/test_node.py -k test_node_api_status_codes 6 passed in 122.16s pytest -v python/ray/dashboard/modules/node/tests/test_actor.py -k test_actor_not_found_status_code 1 passed in 19.74s pytest -q python/ray/dashboard/modules/node/tests/test_actor.py 5 passed in 142.51s pytest -q python/ray/dashboard/modules/node/tests/test_node.py 7 passed, 4 skipped, 2 failed in 286.73s ``` The two failures in the full `test_node.py` run are `test_node_info` and `test_worker_pids_reported`. Both **fail identically against unpatched `node_head.py`** and are pre-existing Windows-environment issues, not regressions: worker cmdlines don't match `"ray::Actor"` on Windows, and runtime_env's uv virtualenv setup hits `WinError 206` (path length). Control run confirming the new tests are not vacuous — against unpatched code: - `/nodes/{unknown}` → `assert 200 == 404` (fails) - `/nodes?view=unknown_view` → `assert 500 == 400` (fails) - `/nodes` → `assert 500 == 400` (fails) - the three success paths → still pass - actor test → `assert 200 == 404`, body `{"result": true, "msg": "Actor details fetched.", "data": {"detail": null}}` (fails) Frontend checks: ``` npx tsc --noEmit # clean, exit 0 npx eslint # clean npx prettier -c # clean ``` Python lint: `ruff check` clean; `black` leaves the changed files unmodified. Caveats worth reviewer attention: all of the above ran on Windows rather than Ray's Linux CI, and against a nightly wheel plus overlaid file rather than a from-source build. Linux CI remains the authoritative check. ### Not a duplicate No open PR references [#51442](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/51442), and the issue timeline has no cross-referenced PRs. The issue has been assigned since 2025-03-18 with no linked work; I commented on it before starting ([comment](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/51442#issuecomment-5084257594)). ### AI assistance AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to produce this change.

signal.title: [Serve] jinja2 imported by haproxy.py but not declared by ray[serve] — slim installs can't import ray.serve
signal.text: ### Ray version `ray==2.57.0` ### Problem `ray/serve/_private/haproxy.py` imports jinja2 at module scope: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/ray-2.57.0/python/ray/serve/_private/haproxy.py#L19 and as of 2.57.0 `controller.py` imports that module unconditionally: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/ray-2.57.0/python/ray/serve/_private/controller.py#L68 so the chain runs on a plain `import ray.serve`, via `__init__.py` -> `api.py` -> `local_testing_mode.py` -> `replica.py` -> `metrics.py` -> `context.py` -> `client.py` -> `controller.py` -> `haproxy.py`. jinja2 isn't declared anywhere in ray's metadata. The `serve` extra pulls `ray-haproxy`: ray-haproxy<2.9.0,>=2.8.25; sys_platform == "linux" and extra == "serve" but that's the HAProxy binary distribution and has `requires_dist: None`, so nothing brings jinja2 in. On a base image that doesn't already have it, `pip install "ray[default,serve]"` produces an install where Serve can't be imported at all: ``` File ".../ray/serve/_private/controller.py", line 68, in <module> from ray.serve._private.haproxy import HAProxyManager File ".../ray/serve/_private/haproxy.py", line 19, in <module> from jinja2 import Environment ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jinja2'. You can run `pip install "ray[serve]"` to install all Ray Serve dependencies. ``` The suggestion in that message is what was already run. 2.56.1 is unaffected, but not because the module is new; `haproxy.py` exists there and imports jinja2 the same way ([2.56.1 L18](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/ray-2.56.1/python/ray/serve/_private/haproxy.py#L18)). Nothing imported it at module scope, so `import ray.serve` never reached it, and 2.56.1 doesn't declare `ray-haproxy` either. 2.57.0 put it on the import path without adding the dependency. This doesn't reproduce on `rayproject/ray:2.57.0`, which carries jinja2 3.1.6 from elsewhere. It only shows up on a slim base. ### Reproduction script ```bash docker run --rm python:3.13-slim bash -c \ 'pip install -q "ray[default,serve]==2.57.0" && python -c "from ray import serve"' ``` ### Suggested fix Declare `jinja2` in the `serve` extra in `python/setup.py`, or move the import inside `HAProxyManager` so it's only required when HAProxy mode is actually used.

signal.title: [core] fix None yield from restarted streaming generator with application errors
signal.text: ## Description Previously, there was a special path in the streaming generator reconstruction: If the retried streaming generator stops with an application exception, it will try to fill `return_objects(0)` for all refs that have not yet been restored. But `return_objects(0)` is `None` if the first streaming generator succeeds. The result is that, in the case of lineage reconstruction, we can see `ray.get(ref)` unexpectedly return `None` if the restarted streaming generator stops with an application exception. This PR removes the special path. We will still treat the exception as the recovered object for the corresponding ref, but if the restarted streaming generator produces a different number of yields than its first execution, the user will get a `StreamingGeneratorReplayInconsistentError` exception on the following `ray.get` instead.
